packageRules.description: mise-managed toolchain tools, minor/patch/digest only — majors (e.g. node 24) need human review and must not join this group. Excludes go: also gomod-relevant, must stay standalone. Excludes flux2: a core library whose minor waits on the Dependency Dashboard (rule 'core pins' below), so it must not share a branch with tools whose minors automerge.

Go module minor bumps not already claimed by a package-name group below. Split from patch/digest (see go-patch below) because Renovate ANDs automerge across every member of one grouped branch — a single minor bump riding along with patch/digest deps on one branch was blocking that branch's automerge entirely. MUST stay before the package-name rules: Renovate applies packageRules in order and a later match overwrites an earlier scalar groupName, so this generic rule would silently absorb kubernetes/sigs.k8s.io/fluxcd/cloudnative-pg/internal updates if it came after them. Excludes go: keep standalone so a Go bump can't red the whole group. Dashboard-gated: no automerge rule matches a minor, so each one used to open as a needs-human PR and wait for a person to merge it. Renovate now opens one only when someone ticks its box on the Dependency Dashboard, and the kubernetes, sigs.k8s.io, fluxcd and cloudnative-pg groups below inherit the gate, since they only rename the group. A security fix still opens unasked: vulnerabilityAlerts forces dependencyDashboardApproval to false, and the top-level vulnerabilityAlerts block merges it.

Go module patch/digest bumps not already claimed by a package-name group below. Split from minor (see go-minor above) so this group never carries a minor member and stays automerge-eligible on its own via the automerge rule near the end of this array. MUST stay before the package-name rules, same reason as go-minor. Excludes go: keep standalone.

Kubernetes core. Grouping follows upstream release cadence. Core library lane: a patch automerges (tail rules), a minor and a major wait on the Dependency Dashboard. The same lane holds for the sigs.k8s.io, fluxcd, cloudnative-pg, external-secrets and helm.sh modules, which need no rule of their own beyond a group. A repository that disables a module keeps it out of every lane, a CVE fix excepted (vulnerabilityAlerts forces it through); the go-deps sync moves those. The top-level separateMinorPatch is what makes this lane work: Renovate reads it at lookup, before any update-type rule, and without it a patch and a minor of one dependency share one bucket, so only the minor is offered and the patch never appears; it also puts a group's patch on its own branch ('patch-kubernetes'), because Renovate automerges a grouped branch only when every member automerges (AND) and holds it back when any member needs dashboard approval (OR).
sigs.k8s.io. Grouping follows upstream release cadence. Core library lane, see the kubernetes group above.
Flux controller APIs are released together and imported as one surface — never bump piecemeal. Core library lane, see the kubernetes group above.
CloudNativePG — the operator, machinery, barman-cloud and the plugin move together upstream. Core library lane, see the kubernetes group above.

First-party libraries. Never automerged: a go-kure/kure bump in a consumer repo carries release-ordering constraints (see the consumer's own guards). Downstream consumers add their own matchers for their own modules in their own config; this preset is public and stays upstream-only. Minor, major and digest wait for a tick on the Dependency Dashboard (a bump nobody may automerge is hand work; the label stays needs-human because a person merges it); a patch opens as a pull request without a tick, see the next rule. The top-level separateMinorPatch keeps the patch branch ('patch-internal') apart from the gated one. A security fix still opens unasked and carries the top-level vulnerabilityAlerts block, so an advisory on a first-party module would automerge: force wins over automerge:false here, and no rule can tell an alert apart.

First-party patch: opens a pull request without a dashboard tick and is never automerged (the rule above sets automerge false and the lane label). A later rule overwrites the gate the previous rule set for every update type.

Core library pins read by a manager other than gomod (a chart or image pin kept by a custom regex manager, the flux2 tool under mise, release pins of the operators): same lane as the Go modules. Minor and major wait on the dashboard; the patch override below lifts the gate for a patch, and the tail rules automerge it. matchDepNames, because a custom manager reports the name it extracts. Extend this list when a consumer adds a core pin of its own.
Core library pin patch and digest (non-gomod): not gated (a digest of these pins opened a pull request before, unchanged); a patch is automerged by the tail rules. Same matcher as the rule above.
GitHub Actions bumps land as chore(ci), matching the commit convention the previous Dependabot config used.

Go itself is excluded from the groups above but must not land unreviewed — a bare Go bump fails each repo's version-consistency checks unless the repo's own sync tooling (scripts/sync-versions.sh) runs alongside it. Dashboard-gate rather than disable, so a security-relevant Go patch stays visible; ticking it still requires the manual sync. allowedVersions admits the 1.27 line, which the repos are moving to, so a repo on 1.27 keeps seeing its patches; it keeps 1.28 unproposed, because moving to the next minor is a coordinated change across the repos, not a bot bump — raise the ceiling with that move. separateMinorPatch keeps a repo still on the previous minor seeing that minor's patches too: without it Renovate puts a 1.26.x patch and the 1.27 move in one non-major bucket and offers only the higher, so the security backports a 1.26 repo needs would vanish from its dashboard. Includes custom.*: the all-managers major gate below has no depName exclusion any more, so it already dashboard-gates a custom-managed go major too — but only this rule carries the allowedVersions ceiling and gates go's minor/patch bumps, which the major gate never sees. A customManagers entry that ever extracted a dependency literally named go needs this rule for that, not just the two built-in managers that track Go's own version today.

The golang base image is the same Go toolchain as the rule above wearing its dockerfile hat — a 1.27→1.28 tag bump is classified minor, so the all-managers major gate below never catches it. Same gate, same patch/minor split and same ceiling as the mise/gomod go rule, raised together with it; matchDepNames golang scopes it to the toolchain image, not every dockerfile dep.

Majors across every manager in use need human review — gomod majors cross the /vN import-path boundary (import rewriting is a human job; +incompatible pre-SIV modules are the exception, gated uniformly anyway), and toolchain/image/npm majors otherwise arrive as ordinary auto-created PRs. Dashboard-gate rather than disable so security-relevant majors stay visible. No !go exclusion here (dropped, was matchDepNames:["!go"]): the two rules above already gate mise/gomod/custom.* deps named go with a stricter allowedVersions pin, and dependencyDashboardApproval is idempotent across matching rules, so re-covering go here is free — it is what closes the same gap for dockerfile/github-actions/npm, which the dedicated Go rules do not match. A customManagers regex/jsonata entry reports here as "custom.<customType>" (e.g. "custom.regex"), never its bare type name — matchManagers is glob-matched, so "custom.*" is what stops a custom-managed major from skipping this gate the way a gomod/mise/dockerfile major cannot. MUST stay before the automerge rules below.

Go testdata trees hold fixtures, never dependencies, but Renovate's :ignoreModulesAndTests default (inherited via config:recommended) skips examples/, test/, tests/ and __fixtures__/ while leaving testdata/ in scope. A fixture that a default manager happens to match — e.g. a values.yaml with a placeholder image, which helm-values extracts — then draws a permanent 'Package lookup failures' block on the Dependency Dashboard, and one carrying a real image would draw a genuine bump PR rewriting the fixture away from its expected output. The guarantee is the ignorePaths entry **/testdata/**, which drops the file at extraction so no dep is ever produced (ignorePaths is mergeable:false, so that list restates the inherited :ignoreModulesAndTests entries in full — and so does the nuget.ignorePaths block, because :ignoreModulesAndTests ships a nuget-level override that keeps test/ and tests/ in scope and getManagerConfig merges it over the top-level list, so without a restated copy the nuget manager would never see the testdata entry; the lane-policy test's drift guard fails if the installed Renovate's own lists ever gain an entry these lack, and its guarantee check fails if any manager-level override, inherited or authored, stops dropping testdata). This rule is the fallback where a consumer's own list replaced this preset's and thereby lost the testdata entry — a consumer's top-level ignorePaths replaces the top-level list for every manager without an override, and a consumer's nuget.ignorePaths replaces the restated nuget one; a top-level consumer value leaves this preset's nuget block intact, since manager objects merge rather than replace: enabled:false then makes Renovate skip the lookup, with no warning and no PR, while the dep still shows under the dashboard's detected dependencies. It is a fallback and not the guarantee because it does not survive a vulnerability alert: Renovate appends the alert's synthetic rule after every authored rule with force:{...vulnerabilityAlerts}, and force.enabled:true both clears the skipReason this rule set and overwrites enabled — verified on 44.14.10, 44.42.0 and 44.65.3, pinned by the lane-policy test's vulnerable-testdata case. **/testdata/** alone already matches a root-level testdata/ as well as a nested one (Renovate 44's matchRegexOrGlob lets a leading ** match zero segments — verified on the same three builds); the second spelling is deliberately redundant, so a future change to that anchoring cannot silently drop root-level trees, and the lane-policy test's root-level case pins the behaviour either way. It sits ahead of the automerge tail so the last-rule invariant on the final rule stays literal.

Automerge for the trusted GitHub Actions lane: go-kure/.github itself, small, widely-used GitHub-maintained actions with a low blast radius (actions/checkout, actions/cache, actions/setup-go, actions/setup-node, actions/download-artifact, actions/upload-artifact), actions/create-github-app-token, and anthropics/claude-code-action. actions/setup-node is the same class as actions/setup-go and was missing from the list. actions/create-github-app-token is GitHub-maintained too, but it takes a GitHub App private key as an input, so it does not meet the low-blast-radius test either: it joins by the owner's decision of 2026-11-20. The other third-party actions the workflows use (sigstore/cosign-installer, peter-evans/rebase, anchore/sbom-action) stay out of the lane. anthropics/claude-code-action is a third-party action that runs a model with a repository secret in the @claude assistant workflow, so it does not meet the low-blast-radius test the others meet: it is on the list because the repository owner decided it joins the lane, and the lane is no longer only GitHub-maintained actions. goreleaser/goreleaser is not an action at all: it is the `version:` pin of goreleaser-action in release-publish.yml, which the github-actions manager reads as that dependency, and it joins by the owner's decision of 2026-11-20. The pin is meant to equal the org-wide REQUIRED_GORELEASER_VERSION (the comment at the pin says so), which is kept outside this repository, so an automerged bump here can lead it until it is moved separately; a consumer that extends this preset and pins goreleaser itself inherits the lane, but the extractVersion rule that keeps the pin bare lives in go-kure/.github's own renovate.json, not in this preset. digest/minor/patch only — a major is excluded by this rule's own matchUpdateTypes, not merely by relying on the dashboard-approval gate above (that gate blocks branch/PR creation, not merging a branch once created). Needs its own groupName, separate from the plain github-actions group below: Renovate ANDs automerge across every member of one grouped branch (see the go-minor rule's description above), and the github-actions group also carries every untrusted third-party action — folding this lane into it would either wrongly automerge a third-party bump riding the same branch, or wrongly hold a trusted bump hostage to one still needing human review. MUST stay before the two automerge rules below so their 'last rule in this preset' invariant stays literal; scoped to matchManagers: ["github-actions"] only, distinct from those rules' gomod/mise scope. A downstream consumer with its own groupName override on any of these depNames (e.g. one re-folding go-kure/.github into a different group for its own vendor-guard tooling) must reconcile that override so it doesn't silently defeat this separation — see go-kure/kure#813.

Automerge: mise toolchain patch/digest, excl. go. Includes flux2: a patch of a core library automerges. Kept as its own rule, not bolted onto the go-version gate rule, because automerge follows the same later-overwrites-earlier merge order as groupName — bolting it on would leak onto every matchPackageNames group above.
Automerge: mise toolchain minor, excl. go and flux2. A flux2 minor is a core library minor and waits on the dashboard (core pins rule), so it is excluded here.

Node from the mise datasource is published before its Docker Hub image, so a bump can name a node:<version>-alpine tag that does not exist yet and the job that pulls it fails with ImagePullBackOff (node 24.22.3 was proposed while the newest image was 24.22.2). Hold the bump for three days so the image exists first. The mise manager only: the dockerfile manager reads the image tags themselves and cannot get ahead of them. It sets no automerge and no group, so it sits ahead of the final rule, which must stay last.

Automerge: gomod patch/digest, excl. go and the first-party group — matches only the go-patch group above (never go-minor, since that group never contains a patch/digest member). Includes the core library modules (k8s.io, sigs.k8s.io, fluxcd, cloudnative-pg, external-secrets, helm): a core digest stays automerged, as before, because several core modules are pseudo-version modules. The automerge rules are the tail of this array and each excludes explicitly what it must not take, so none depends on rule order. A downstream consumer that adds its own first-party matchers must exclude them here too, by appending a rule that sets automerge false for them (later rules overwrite earlier scalars).

Automerge: a patch of everything else — npm, container images, compose files, custom regex pins — and of the core library pins a custom manager reads. Not gomod (the rule above) and not mise (the two rules above), not GitHub Actions (only the trusted lane automerges an Action, because an untrusted Action runs with the repository's token and a patch tag can be retargeted: the tj-actions incident), not go or golang (dashboard-gated by their own rules), not the first-party modules. A minor of the same dependencies opens a pull request for a hand merge, a major waits on the dashboard. Must stay a tail rule: it relies on its own exclusions, not on order.
